candidates.title: Gannet colony walk on Bonaventure Island
candidates.summary: Walking trails across Bonaventure Island to one of the world's largest gannet colonies, a memorable wildlife sight for kids. Trail lengths vary; access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Percé glass-floor lookout (Géoparc)
candidates.summary: Suspended glass platform on Mont Sainte-Anne with views over Percé Rock; short and kid-friendly. Accessibility not verified since access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Cap-Gaspé Lands End trail, Forillon
candidates.summary: Classic Forillon trail to the lighthouse at the tip of the peninsula, with chances to see seals and whales; moderate length suits the family. Access needs not answered.

candidates.title: Whale-watching cruise from Grande-Grave

candidates.title: Grande-Grave heritage site, Forillon
candidates.summary: Restored fishing-village buildings with interpretation of Gaspé cod-fishing life; easy and good for breaking up driving days.

candidatesAccepted.summary: Covers the requested Percé Rock stop. The cruise passes close to the rock and lands at the gannet colony. The band assumes 2 adult and 2 child boat fares plus SÉPAQ park entry, at prices that are not confirmed for 2027. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Parc national du Bic short walks as a break stop
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short, cheap leg-stretch on the south-shore route, which gives the 7-year-old a break and avoids the north shore they have already done. The band assumes SÉPAQ daily adult entry, with children free.

candidatesAccepted.title: Serviced campsite with showers in a Gaspésie park
candidatesAccepted.summary: Keeps lodging within budget while meeting the shower rule. The band assumes a family site with showers in a SÉPAQ or Parks Canada campground, using their own tent and car. The price is per night, and July sites fill fast.
